summaryI18n.zh: 按主题、作者或引用关系检索、发现学术论文（只负责找，不写综述）
summaryI18n.en: Search & discover academic papers by topic, author, or citations (finding only, not writing)

scenarioAgent.name: lit-search
scenarioAgent.description: Literature search & discovery agent — route here whenever the user wants to find, search, look up, retrieve, discover, locate, fetch, or pull up academic papers / publications / studies / articles / references / literature, in any phrasing or language. Covers three intent classes: (a) topical / keyword queries — 'papers about X', 'find studies on Y', 'recent work in Z', 'state of the art in W', author / venue / year-range filters, 'collect background on Q', 'what's the literature on…'; (b) exact identifier lookups — PMID, DOI, arXiv ID, ISBN, single known-paper retrieval; (c) citation tracing — 'who cited this', 'what does it cite', 'related work', forward / backward snowball, reference expansion from one or more seed papers. Trigger even when the search verb is implicit — 'I'm starting a project on X', 'help me get up to speed on Y', 'gather sources for Z' all imply a topical query. Do NOT use for: writing a review or synthesis from an already-curated paper set (route to `lit-review`); deep-reading or summarising a specific paper the user has already opened (handle directly via Read / paper MCP). Outputs a structured PLAN that dispatches the built-in `searcher` / `citation-explorer` sub-agents, scores the candidates server-side via the `score_window` tool, and writes the closing summary after results return.

subAgents.name: searcher
subAgents.description: Search executor. Invokes the deterministic `retrieve` MCP tool once with the planner's brief (keywords / method / object / sources). Query shaping, fan-out, dedup, enrichment and F22 scoring all happen server-side in `retrieve`; the searcher does not compose query matrices. Use when the task requires retrieving a topic's literature.

subAgents.name: citation-explorer
subAgents.description: Citation explorer. Performs forward / backward snowball lookup from one or more seed papers (PMID / DOI / workspace handle), deduplicates, and returns the new citation set as candidates. Use when the user explicitly asks "who cited this" / "what does it cite" / "trace citations" AND a seed paper is indicated.
